## The step API of `agentica test`.
##
## A step program builds a list of steps with `step` and passes it to `run`. A handler gets the context of its scenario
## and returns it: most functions here take the context first and return it, so keep the one they return.

struct Settings
  base: String
  agentica: List[String]
  allow_run: Bool
  seeded: Bool
  seed: Int
end

struct StepLine
  index: Int
  definition: Int
  pattern: String
  captures: List[String]
  has_doc: Bool
  doc: String
  has_table: Bool
  table: List[List[String]]
end

enum Program
  NotStarted
  Running(Process)
end

struct Scenario
  settings: Settings
  state: Map[String, Json]
  step: StepLine
  program: Program
end

## The state of one scenario: the values saved with `set`, the current step and the program under test.
export struct Context
  ## The scenario's state.
  scenario: Scenario
end

## A step definition: a pattern and the handler that runs for the steps that match it. Build one with `step`.
export struct Step
  ## The step text to match. `{string}` and `{int}` capture a value.
  pattern: String
  ## Gets the context and the captured values as strings, in order, and returns the context.
  handler: Fn[Context, List[String], Context]
end

## Returns a step that runs `handler` for the steps whose text matches `pattern`.
export def step(pattern: String, handler: Fn[Context, List[String], Context]) -> Step
  return Step(pattern: pattern, handler: handler)
end

## Serves the steps that `agentica test` asks for, with the built-in steps added in front of `steps`. It never returns.
## Run any other way, it prints how to run the step program and exits with code 2.
export def run(steps: List[Step]) -> Void
  all = predefined().concat(steps)
  args = System.args()
  mode = ""
  if args.size == 2 and args[0] == "--agentica-bdd"
    mode = args[1]
  end
  if mode == "list"
    check_tasks()
    all.each do |item|
      fields: Map[String, Json] = {"event": JSON.from("step"), "pattern": JSON.from(item.pattern)}
      deliver(record_text(fields))
    end
    emit("ready")
    System.exit(0)
  elsif mode == "scenario"
    check_tasks()
    serve(all)
  end
  IO.warn("run this step program with agentica test --steps FILE")
  System.exit(2)
end

## Returns the Doc String under the current step. Ends the scenario with an error when the step has none.
export def doc_string(ctx: Context) -> String
  if ctx.scenario.step.has_doc
    return ctx.scenario.step.doc
  end
  halt("RUNTIME-BDD-CONTEXT", "this step has no Doc String")
  return ""
end

## Returns the Data Table under the current step as rows of cells. Ends the scenario with an error when the step has
## none.
export def table(ctx: Context) -> List[List[String]]
  rows: List[List[String]] = ctx.scenario.step.table
  if not ctx.scenario.step.has_table
    halt("RUNTIME-BDD-CONTEXT", "this step has no Data Table")
  end
  return rows
end

## Fails the scenario with `message` when `condition` is false. Returns the context.
export def assert(ctx: Context, condition: Bool, message: String) -> Context
  emit("assert")
  if not condition
    halt("RUNTIME-BDD-ASSERTION", message)
  end
  return ctx
end

## Returns the context with `value` saved under `name`, for the later steps of the same scenario.
export def set(ctx: Context, name: String, value: Json) -> Context
  return with_state(ctx, ctx.scenario.state.put(name, value))
end

## Returns the value saved under `name`, or an error when there is none.
export def get(ctx: Context, name: String) -> Result[Json]
  if ctx.scenario.state.has_key?(name)
    return ctx.scenario.state.get(name)
  end
  return error("missing scenario state")
end

## Starts the Agentica program at `path`, relative to the feature file, and returns the context that holds it. One
## program may start per scenario.
export def given_program(ctx: Context, path: String) -> Context
  case ctx.scenario.program
    Program.Running(_) -> halt("RUNTIME-BDD-CONTEXT", "only one program may start per scenario")
    Program.NotStarted -> return start(ctx, path)
  end
  return ctx
end

## Sends `text` and a newline to the program's input.
export def when_line(ctx: Context, text: String) -> Context
  return send(ctx, "#{text}\n")
end

## Sends `text` to the program's input as it is.
export def when_input(ctx: Context, text: String) -> Context
  return send(ctx, text)
end

## Closes the program's input.
export def when_eof(ctx: Context) -> Context
  p = program(ctx)
  closed = Process.close_stdin(p, 5000)
  check(closed.ok?, closed.message)
  return ctx
end

## Checks that the next output line of the program is `expected`, waiting up to `timeout_ms` milliseconds.
export def then_line(ctx: Context, expected: String, timeout_ms: Int) -> Context
  return compare_text(ctx, read_line(ctx, timeout_ms), expected)
end

## Checks that the next output line and `expected` are the same JSON value, in any key order, waiting up to
## `timeout_ms` milliseconds.
export def then_json_line(ctx: Context, expected: String, timeout_ms: Int) -> Context
  actual = read_line(ctx, timeout_ms)
  left = JSON.parse(expected)
  right = JSON.parse(actual)
  if not left.ok? or not right.ok?
    halt("RUNTIME-BDD-JSON", "expected and received lines must be valid JSON")
    return ctx
  end
  return compare(ctx, Test.eq(right.unwrap!, left.unwrap!), JSON.encode(left.unwrap!), JSON.encode(right.unwrap!))
end

## Checks that the program is still running with its input open.
export def then_stdin_open(ctx: Context) -> Context
  p = program(ctx)
  wanted = "open stdin and active program"
  state = "closed stdin or stopped program"
  if Process.send(p, "", 5000).ok? and not Process.wait(p, 1).ok?
    state = wanted
  end
  return compare(ctx, Test.eq(state, wanted), wanted, state)
end

## Waits up to `timeout_ms` milliseconds for the program to exit and checks that its exit code is `code`.
export def then_exit(ctx: Context, code: Int, timeout_ms: Int) -> Context
  p = program(ctx)
  positive(timeout_ms)
  status = Process.wait(p, timeout_ms)
  check(status.ok?, status.message)
  finished(p)
  actual = status.unwrap!
  return compare(ctx, Test.eq(actual, code), code.inspect, actual.inspect)
end

## Checks that the output no line step has read yet is `expected`. The program must have exited.
export def then_stdout(ctx: Context, expected: String) -> Context
  return compare_text(ctx, finished(exited(program(ctx))).stdout, expected)
end

## Checks that the whole error output is `expected`. The program must have exited.
export def then_stderr(ctx: Context, expected: String) -> Context
  return compare_text(ctx, finished(exited(program(ctx))).stderr, expected)
end

def predefined() -> List[Step]
  return [
    step("the Agentica program {string}") do |ctx, args| given_program(ctx, args[0]) end,
    step("I send a line:") do |ctx, args| when_line(ctx, doc_string(ctx)) end,
    step("I send the line {string}") do |ctx, args| when_line(ctx, args[0]) end,
    step("I send input:") do |ctx, args| when_input(ctx, doc_string(ctx)) end,
    step("I close stdin") do |ctx, args| when_eof(ctx) end,
    step("I receive a line within {int} milliseconds:") do |ctx, args|
      then_line(ctx, doc_string(ctx), args[0].to_i!)
    end,
    step("I receive the line {string} within {int} milliseconds") do |ctx, args|
      then_line(ctx, args[0], args[1].to_i!)
    end,
    step("I receive a JSON line within {int} milliseconds:") do |ctx, args|
      then_json_line(ctx, doc_string(ctx), args[0].to_i!)
    end,
    step("stdin remains open") do |ctx, args| then_stdin_open(ctx) end,
    step("the program exits with code {int} within {int} milliseconds") do |ctx, args|
      then_exit(ctx, args[0].to_i!, args[1].to_i!)
    end,
    step("stdout is:") do |ctx, args| then_stdout(ctx, doc_string(ctx)) end,
    step("stderr is:") do |ctx, args| then_stderr(ctx, doc_string(ctx)) end,
  ]
end

# One step per channel line until the runner closes the channel; a failure has already ended the run with a fail
# record.
def serve(all: List[Step]) -> Void
  init = Process.parent_read_line(idle_ms())
  if not init.ok?
    System.exit(0)
  end
  settings = JSON.decode(init.unwrap!, Settings)
  if not settings.ok?
    halt("RUNTIME-BDD-INFRA", "invalid scenario settings: #{settings.message}")
  end
  empty: List[List[String]] = []
  blank = StepLine(
    index: 0,
    definition: 0,
    pattern: "",
    captures: [],
    has_doc: false,
    doc: "",
    has_table: false,
    table: empty,
  )
  ctx = Context(scenario: Scenario(settings: settings.unwrap!, state: {}, step: blank, program: Program.NotStarted))
  line = Process.parent_read_line(idle_ms())
  while line.ok?
    found = JSON.decode(line.unwrap!, StepLine)
    if not found.ok?
      halt("RUNTIME-BDD-INFRA", "invalid step line: #{found.message}")
    end
    current = found.unwrap!
    if current.definition < 0 or current.definition >= all.size or all[current.definition].pattern != current.pattern
      halt("RUNTIME-BDD-INFRA", "the step program built a different list of steps: #{current.pattern}")
    end
    ctx = all[current.definition].handler.call(with_step(ctx, current), current.captures)
    if Task.pending_count() > 0
      halt("RUNTIME-BDD-PENDING-TASKS", "await pending tasks before returning from a BDD handler")
    end
    check_crash()
    probe(ctx)
    fields: Map[String, Json] = {"event": JSON.from("end"), "index": JSON.from(current.index)}
    deliver(record_text(fields))
    line = Process.parent_read_line(idle_ms())
  end
  System.exit(0)
end

def check_tasks() -> Void
  if Task.pending_count() > 0
    halt("RUNTIME-BDD-PENDING-TASKS", "await pending tasks before calling BDD.run")
  end
  check_crash()
end

def check_crash() -> Void
  crash = Task.unobserved_crash()
  if crash.ok?
    halt("RUNTIME-TASK-CRASHED", crash.unwrap!)
  end
end

def probe(ctx: Context) -> Void
  case ctx.scenario.program
    Program.Running(p) ->
      peek = Process.read_bytes(p, 0, 1000)
      if not peek.ok? and peek.message == over_text()
        halt("RUNTIME-BDD-OUTPUT-LIMIT", "program output exceeds 1 MiB")
      end
    Program.NotStarted -> return
  end
end

def start(ctx: Context, path: String) -> Context
  settings = ctx.scenario.settings
  joined: Result[String] = ok(path)
  if not path.start_with?("/")
    joined = Path.join([settings.base, path])
  end
  file = Path.resolve(joined.unwrap_or(path)).unwrap_or(path)
  info = File.stat(file, 5000)
  if not (info.ok? and file.end_with?(".agc")) or info.unwrap!.kind != "file"
    halt("RUNTIME-BDD-PROGRAM", "expected an existing .agc program")
  end
  if settings.agentica.size == 0
    halt("RUNTIME-BDD-INFRA", "Agentica executable is unavailable")
  end
  flags: List[String] = []
  if settings.allow_run
    flags = ["--allow-run"]
  end
  if settings.seeded
    flags = flags.concat(["--seed", settings.seed.to_s])
  end
  args = settings.agentica.drop(1).concat(flags).concat(["--max-steps", "1000000", file])
  spawned = Process.spawn_captured(settings.agentica[0], args, settings.base, 30000)
  if not spawned.ok?
    if spawned.message == "process: executable is unavailable"
      halt("RUNTIME-BDD-INFRA", "Agentica executable is unavailable")
    end
    halt("RUNTIME-BDD-IO", spawned.message)
  end
  return Context(scenario: Scenario(settings: settings, state: ctx.scenario.state, step: ctx.scenario.step,
                                    program: Program.Running(spawned.unwrap!)))
end

def program(ctx: Context) -> Process
  found: Result[Process] = error("start a program before using its streams")
  case ctx.scenario.program
    Program.Running(p) -> found = ok(p)
    Program.NotStarted -> halt("RUNTIME-BDD-CONTEXT", found.message)
  end
  return found.unwrap!
end

def send(ctx: Context, text: String) -> Context
  sent = Process.send(program(ctx), text, 5000)
  if not sent.ok? and sent.message == "process: stdin is closed"
    halt("RUNTIME-BDD-CONTEXT", "stdin is already closed")
  end
  check(sent.ok?, sent.message)
  return ctx
end

def read_line(ctx: Context, timeout_ms: Int) -> String
  p = program(ctx)
  positive(timeout_ms)
  line = Process.read_line(p, timeout_ms)
  if not line.ok? and line.message == "process: end of input"
    halt("RUNTIME-BDD-ASSERTION", "stdout ended before the expected line")
  end
  check(line.ok?, line.message)
  return line.unwrap!
end

def exited(p: Process) -> Process
  if not Process.wait(p, 1).ok?
    halt("RUNTIME-BDD-CONTEXT", "complete output requires program exit")
  end
  return p
end

def finished(p: Process) -> ProcessOutput
  output = Process.output(p, 5000)
  check(output.ok?, output.message)
  if output.unwrap!.truncated
    halt("RUNTIME-BDD-OUTPUT-LIMIT", "program output exceeds 1 MiB")
  end
  return output.unwrap!
end

def positive(timeout_ms: Int) -> Void
  if timeout_ms <= 0
    halt("RUNTIME-BDD-TIMEOUT", "timeout must be a positive integer")
  end
end

# Ends the scenario child with a fail record for a failed stream operation.
def check(fine: Bool, message: String) -> Void
  if fine
    return
  end
  if message == "network: operation timed out"
    halt("RUNTIME-BDD-TIMEOUT", "BDD operation timed out")
  elsif message == over_text() or message == "process: line exceeds 1048576 bytes"
    halt("RUNTIME-BDD-OUTPUT-LIMIT", "program output exceeds 1 MiB")
  end
  halt("RUNTIME-BDD-IO", message)
end

def compare_text(ctx: Context, actual: String, expected: String) -> Context
  return compare(ctx, Test.eq(actual, expected), expected.inspect, actual.inspect)
end

def compare(ctx: Context, checked: Result[Void], expected: String, actual: String) -> Context
  emit("assert")
  if not checked.ok?
    fields: Map[String, Json] = {
      "event": JSON.from("fail"),
      "code": JSON.from("RUNTIME-BDD-ASSERTION"),
      "message": JSON.from("BDD assertion failed"),
      "expected": JSON.from(clip(expected)),
      "actual": JSON.from(clip(actual)),
    }
    finish(fields)
  end
  return ctx
end

def clip(text: String) -> String
  if text.length <= 65536
    return text
  end
  return "#{text.slice(0, 65536)}... (#{text.length - 65536} more characters)"
end

def with_state(ctx: Context, state: Map[String, Json]) -> Context
  return Context(scenario: Scenario(settings: ctx.scenario.settings, state: state, step: ctx.scenario.step,
                                    program: ctx.scenario.program))
end

def with_step(ctx: Context, current: StepLine) -> Context
  return Context(scenario: Scenario(settings: ctx.scenario.settings, state: ctx.scenario.state, step: current,
                                    program: ctx.scenario.program))
end

def halt(code: String, message: String) -> Void
  fields: Map[String, Json] = {"event": JSON.from("fail"), "code": JSON.from(code), "message": JSON.from(message)}
  finish(fields)
end

def finish(fields: Map[String, Json]) -> Void
  deliver(record_text(fields))
  System.exit(1)
end

def emit(event: String) -> Void
  fields: Map[String, Json] = {"event": JSON.from(event)}
  deliver(record_text(fields))
end

def deliver(text: String) -> Void
  IO.flush()
  sent = Process.parent_send(text, send_ms())
  if not sent.ok?
    if sent.message == "process: send exceeds 1048576 bytes"
      fields: Map[String, Json] = {
        "event": JSON.from("fail"),
        "code": JSON.from("RUNTIME-BDD-OUTPUT-LIMIT"),
        "message": JSON.from("handler output exceeds 1 MiB"),
      }
      Process.parent_send(record_text(fields), send_ms())
    else
      IO.warn("BDD could not send a record to the runner: #{sent.message}")
    end
    System.exit(1)
  end
end

def idle_ms() -> Int
  return 86400000
end

def send_ms() -> Int
  return 5000
end

def record_text(fields: Map[String, Json]) -> String
  return "#{JSON.encode(JSON.object(fields))}\n"
end

def over_text() -> String
  return "process: output exceeds 1048576 bytes"
end

## Reads Gherkin feature files for `agentica test`.
##
## It supports `Feature`, `Background`, `Scenario`, `Scenario Outline` with `Examples`, tags, Doc Strings and Data
## Tables, in English only.

import Report from "std/test/report"

## A problem in a feature file: a code, a message and its place.
export struct Diagnostic
  code: String
  message: String
  span: Report.Span
end

## The result of a read that can fail: `Done` with a value, or `Failed` with a `Diagnostic`.
export enum Outcome[T]
  Done(T)
  Failed(Diagnostic)
end

## What follows a step: nothing, a Doc String or a Data Table.
export enum Argument
  NoArgument
  DocString(String)
  DataTable(List[List[String]])
end

## One step of a scenario: its kind (`Given`, `When` or `Then`), the text after the keyword, its argument and its
## place.
export struct Step
  kind: String
  text: String
  argument: Argument
  span: Report.Span
end

## One scenario, with the `Background` steps first, the tags of the feature, of the scenario and of its `Examples`
## block, and the example row it came from.
export struct Scenario
  name: String
  steps: List[Step]
  tags: List[String]
  span: Report.Span
  example: Report.Example
end

## A parsed feature file. A `Scenario Outline` is already expanded into one scenario for each `Examples` row.
export struct Feature
  name: String
  scenarios: List[Scenario]
  tags: List[String]
  span: Report.Span
end

struct Source
  file: String
  raws: List[String]
  texts: List[String]
end

struct ExampleRow
  span: Report.Span
  bindings: Map[String, String]
  tags: List[String]
end

struct Draft
  name: String
  outline: Bool
  steps: List[Step]
  examples: List[ExampleRow]
  tags: List[String]
  span: Report.Span
end

struct TableRow
  span: Report.Span
  cells: List[String]
end

struct Table
  rows: List[TableRow]
  next: Int
end

struct Doc
  text: String
  next: Int
end

## Parses the text of the feature file `file`. Returns the `Feature`, or a `Diagnostic` for the first problem.
export def parse(file: String, text: String) -> Outcome[Feature]
  src = read_lines(file, text)
  count = src.raws.size
  cursor = 0
  title = ""
  has_title = false
  title_span = location(src, 0)
  feature_tags: List[String] = []
  pending: List[String] = []
  background: List[Step] = []
  has_background = false
  drafts: List[Draft] = []
  current = Draft(name: "", outline: false, steps: [], examples: [], tags: [], span: title_span)
  has_current = false
  mode = ""
  previous = ""
  while cursor < count
    line = src.texts[cursor]
    where = location(src, cursor)
    heading = heading_keyword(line)
    action = step_keyword(line)
    if line == "" or line.start_with?("#")
      if line.start_with?("# language:") and line != "# language: en"
        return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-UNSUPPORTED", "only English Gherkin is supported", where)
      end
      cursor += 1
    elsif line.start_with?("@")
      if not tags?(line)
        return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-TAGS", "invalid tags", where)
      end
      pending = pending.concat(split_tags(line))
      cursor += 1
    elsif heading != ""
      name = drop_blanks(rest_of(line, heading.length + 1))
      if name == "" and heading != "Examples" and heading != "Background"
        return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-HEADER", "a section needs a name", where)
      end
      if heading == "Feature"
        if has_title
          return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-HEADER", "one Feature is allowed per file", where)
        end
        title = name
        has_title = true
        title_span = where
        feature_tags = pending
        pending = []
        cursor += 1
      elsif not has_title
        return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-HEADER", "Feature must come first", where)
      elsif heading == "Background"
        if has_background or has_current or pending.size > 0
          return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-HEADER", "Background must occur once before scenarios, without tags", where)
        end
        has_background = true
        mode = "background"
        previous = ""
        cursor += 1
      elsif heading == "Examples"
        if not (has_current and current.outline)
          return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-EXAMPLES", "Examples requires a Scenario Outline", where)
        end
        example_tags = pending
        pending = []
        cursor += 1
        while cursor < count and (src.texts[cursor] == "" or src.texts[cursor].start_with?("#"))
          cursor += 1
        end
        block = Table(rows: [], next: cursor)
        case read_table(src, cursor)
          Outcome.Done(found) -> block = found
          Outcome.Failed(problem) -> return Outcome.Failed(problem)
        end
        cursor = block.next
        if block.rows.size < 2
          return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-EXAMPLES", "Examples needs a header and at least one row", where)
        end
        headers = block.rows[0].cells
        if not unique_names?(headers)
          return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-EXAMPLES", "Examples headers must be nonempty and unique", where)
        end
        rows = current.examples
        for row in block.rows.drop(1)
          rows = rows.push(ExampleRow(span: row.span, bindings: bind(headers, row.cells), tags: example_tags))
        end
        current = with_examples(current, rows)
        mode = "examples"
      else
        if has_current
          drafts = drafts.push(current)
        end
        current = Draft(
          name: name,
          outline: heading == "Scenario Outline",
          steps: [],
          examples: [],
          tags: pending,
          span: where,
        )
        has_current = true
        pending = []
        mode = "scenario"
        previous = ""
        cursor += 1
      end
    elsif action != ""
      if mode != "background" and mode != "scenario"
        return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-STEP", "a step requires Background or Scenario", where)
      end
      if pending.size > 0
        return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-TAGS", "tags must precede a section", where)
      end
      kind = action
      if action == "And" or action == "But"
        kind = previous
      end
      if kind == ""
        return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-STEP", "And or But needs a preceding step", where)
      end
      previous = kind
      step = Step(
        kind: kind,
        text: drop_blanks(rest_of(line, action.length)),
        argument: Argument.NoArgument,
        span: where,
      )
      if mode == "background"
        background = background.push(step)
      else
        current = with_steps(current, current.steps.push(step))
      end
      cursor += 1
    elsif line.start_with?("\"\"\"") or line.start_with?("|")
      argument = Argument.NoArgument
      if line.start_with?("|")
        block = Table(rows: [], next: cursor)
        case read_table(src, cursor)
          Outcome.Done(found) -> block = found
          Outcome.Failed(problem) -> return Outcome.Failed(problem)
        end
        cursor = block.next
        argument = Argument.DataTable(block.rows.map do |row| row.cells end)
      else
        doc = Doc(text: "", next: cursor)
        case read_doc(src, cursor)
          Outcome.Done(found) -> doc = found
          Outcome.Failed(problem) -> return Outcome.Failed(problem)
        end
        cursor = doc.next
        argument = Argument.DocString(doc.text)
      end
      here = location(src, cursor)
      if (mode != "background" and mode != "scenario") or pending.size > 0
        return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-ARGUMENT", "step argument is outside a step", here)
      end
      active = active_steps(mode, background, current, has_current)
      if active.size == 0 or has_argument?(active[active.size - 1])
        return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-ARGUMENT", "a step accepts one Doc String or Data Table", here)
      end
      last = active[active.size - 1]
      active = active.set(active.size - 1, Step(kind: last.kind, text: last.text, argument: argument, span: last.span))
      if mode == "background"
        background = active
      else
        current = with_steps(current, active)
      end
    elsif unsupported?(line)
      return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-UNSUPPORTED", "unsupported or invalid Gherkin syntax", where)
    else
      if (
        not has_title or
        active_steps(mode, background, current, has_current).size > 0 or
        pending.size > 0 or
        mode == "examples"
      )
        return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-STEP", "unexpected text after steps", where)
      end
      cursor += 1
    end
  end
  if not has_title
    return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-HEADER", "missing Feature", location(src, 0))
  end
  if pending.size > 0
    return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-TAGS", "tags without a section", location(src, 0))
  end
  if not has_current
    return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-EMPTY", "Feature needs at least one scenario", title_span)
  end
  if has_background and background.size == 0
    return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-EMPTY", "Background needs steps", title_span)
  end
  drafts = drafts.push(current)
  scenarios: List[Scenario] = []
  for draft in drafts
    if draft.steps.size == 0
      return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-EMPTY", "Scenario needs steps", draft.span)
    end
    if draft.outline and draft.examples.size == 0
      return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-EXAMPLES", "Scenario Outline needs Examples", draft.span)
    end
    steps = background.concat(draft.steps)
    tags = feature_tags.concat(draft.tags)
    if draft.outline
      for row in draft.examples
        expanded = expand_row(draft, steps, tags, row)
        if not expanded.ok?
          return fail("PARSE-GHERKIN-PARAMETER", "no value for <#{expanded.message}>", row.span)
        end
        scenarios = scenarios.push(expanded.unwrap!)
      end
    else
      scenarios = scenarios.push(
        Scenario(name: draft.name, steps: steps, tags: tags, span: draft.span, example: Report.Example.NoExample),
      )
    end
  end
  return Outcome.Done(Feature(name: title, scenarios: scenarios, tags: feature_tags, span: title_span))
end

def problem(code: String, message: String, span: Report.Span) -> Diagnostic
  return Diagnostic(code: code, message: message, span: span)
end

def fail(code: String, message: String, span: Report.Span) -> Outcome[Feature]
  return Outcome.Failed(problem(code, message, span))
end

def read_lines(file: String, text: String) -> Source
  raws = text.split("\n").map do |part|
    if part.end_with?("\r")
      return part.slice(0, part.length - 1)
    end
    part
  end
  return Source(file: file, raws: raws, texts: raws.map do |raw| raw.strip end)
end

# A location covers its whole raw line; past the end it is the last line.
def location(src: Source, index: Int) -> Report.Span
  at = index
  if at >= src.raws.size
    at = src.raws.size - 1
  end
  return Report.Span(file: src.file, line: at + 1, column: 1, end_column: src.raws[at].length + 1)
end

def rest_of(text: String, start: Int) -> String
  return text.slice(start, text.length - start)
end

def blank_prefix(text: String) -> Int
  count = 0
  for c in text.split("")
    if c != " " and c != "\t"
      return count
    end
    count += 1
  end
  return count
end

def drop_blanks(text: String) -> String
  return rest_of(text, blank_prefix(text))
end

def heading_keyword(line: String) -> String
  colon = line.index_of(":")
  if not colon.ok?
    return ""
  end
  word = line.slice(0, colon.unwrap!)
  if (
    word == "Feature" or
    word == "Background" or
    word == "Scenario Outline" or
    word == "Scenario" or
    word == "Example" or
    word == "Examples"
  )
    return word
  end
  return ""
end

def step_keyword(line: String) -> String
  word = line.replace("\t", " ").split(" ")[0]
  if (
    word.length < line.length and
    (word == "Given" or word == "When" or word == "Then" or word == "And" or word == "But")
  )
    return word
  end
  return ""
end

def unsupported?(line: String) -> Bool
  for prefix in ["Rule:", "Scenario Template:", "Scenarios:", "* ", "```", "Given:", "When:", "Then:", "And:", "But:"]
    if line.start_with?(prefix)
      return true
    end
  end
  return false
end

def tags?(line: String) -> Bool
  for tag in line.replace("\t", " ").split(" ")
    if tag != "" and (tag.length < 2 or not tag.start_with?("@"))
      return false
    end
  end
  return true
end

def split_tags(line: String) -> List[String]
  spaced = line.replace("\t", " ").replace("\r", " ").replace(String.from_code(12), " ")
  return spaced.split(" ").filter do |tag| tag != "" end
end

def doc_delimiter?(line: String) -> Bool
  allowed = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789_./+-"
  for c in rest_of(line, 3).split("")
    if not allowed.include?(c)
      return false
    end
  end
  return true
end

def unique_names?(names: List[String]) -> Bool
  seen: Map[String, Bool] = {}
  for name in names
    if name == "" or seen.has_key?(name)
      return false
    end
    seen = seen.put(name, true)
  end
  return true
end

def bind(headers: List[String], cells: List[String]) -> Map[String, String]
  bindings: Map[String, String] = {}
  for i in 0...headers.size
    bindings = bindings.put(headers[i], cells[i])
  end
  return bindings
end

def with_steps(draft: Draft, steps: List[Step]) -> Draft
  return Draft(
    name: draft.name,
    outline: draft.outline,
    steps: steps,
    examples: draft.examples,
    tags: draft.tags,
    span: draft.span,
  )
end

def with_examples(draft: Draft, rows: List[ExampleRow]) -> Draft
  return Draft(
    name: draft.name,
    outline: draft.outline,
    steps: draft.steps,
    examples: rows,
    tags: draft.tags,
    span: draft.span,
  )
end

def active_steps(mode: String, background: List[Step], current: Draft, has_current: Bool) -> List[Step]
  if mode == "background"
    return background
  end
  if has_current
    return current.steps
  end
  return []
end

def has_argument?(step: Step) -> Bool
  case step.argument
    Argument.NoArgument -> return false
    _ -> return true
  end
end

def read_table(src: Source, start: Int) -> Outcome[Table]
  rows: List[TableRow] = []
  width = 0
  cursor = start
  while cursor < src.texts.size and src.texts[cursor].start_with?("|")
    where = location(src, cursor)
    cells = table_row(src.texts[cursor])
    if not cells.ok?
      return Outcome.Failed(problem("PARSE-GHERKIN-TABLE", cells.message, where))
    end
    found = cells.unwrap!
    if rows.size == 0
      width = found.size
    end
    if found.size != width
      return Outcome.Failed(problem("PARSE-GHERKIN-TABLE", "table rows must have the same width", where))
    end
    rows = rows.push(TableRow(span: where, cells: found))
    cursor += 1
  end
  return Outcome.Done(Table(rows: rows, next: cursor))
end

# Each content line loses the opening line's indentation, at most.
def read_doc(src: Source, start: Int) -> Outcome[Doc]
  where = location(src, start)
  opening = src.texts[start]
  indent = String.index_of(src.raws[start], opening).unwrap_or(0)
  if not doc_delimiter?(opening)
    return Outcome.Failed(problem("PARSE-GHERKIN-ARGUMENT", "invalid Doc String delimiter", where))
  end
  cursor = start + 1
  while cursor < src.texts.size and src.texts[cursor] != "\"\"\""
    cursor += 1
  end
  if cursor >= src.texts.size
    return Outcome.Failed(problem("PARSE-GHERKIN-ARGUMENT", "unterminated Doc String", where))
  end
  content = src.raws.take(cursor).drop(start + 1).map do |value|
    blanks = blank_prefix(value)
    if indent < blanks
      return rest_of(value, indent)
    end
    rest_of(value, blanks)
  end
  return Outcome.Done(Doc(text: content.join("\n"), next: cursor + 1))
end

def table_row(row: String) -> Result[List[String]]
  if not row.end_with?("|")
    return error("a table row must end with |")
  end
  body = rest_of(row, 1)
  chars = body.split("")
  ends = (0...chars.size).to_a.filter do |i| chars[i] == "|" and even_run?(chars, i) end
  starts = [0].concat(ends.map do |i| i + 1 end)
  raws = (0...ends.size).to_a.map do |k| body.slice(starts[k], ends[k] - starts[k]) end
  rest = rest_of(body, starts[ends.size])
  cells = collect(raws.concat([rest]).map(&unescape_cell))
  if not cells.ok?
    return cells
  end
  if rest != ""
    return error("a table row must end with an unescaped |")
  end
  if ends.size == 0
    return error("a table row needs at least one cell")
  end
  return ok(cells.unwrap!.take(ends.size).map do |cell| cell.strip end)
end

def even_run?(chars: List[String], at: Int) -> Bool
  i = at
  while i > 0 and chars[i - 1] == "\\"
    i -= 1
  end
  return (at - i) % 2 == 0
end

def unescape_cell(raw: String) -> Result[String]
  parts = raw.split("\\\\").map do |part| part.replace("\\|", "|").replace("\\n", "\n") end
  if parts.any? do |part| part.include?("\\") end
    return error("invalid table escape")
  end
  return ok(parts.join("\\"))
end

def collect(results: List[Result[String]]) -> Result[List[String]]
  for result in results
    if not result.ok?
      return error(result.message)
    end
  end
  return ok(results.map do |result| result.unwrap! end)
end

def expand_row(draft: Draft, steps: List[Step], tags: List[String], row: ExampleRow) -> Result[Scenario]
  name = try substitute(draft.name, row.bindings)
  expanded: List[Step] = []
  for step in steps
    text = try substitute(step.text, row.bindings)
    argument = try substitute_argument(step.argument, row.bindings)
    expanded = expanded.push(Step(kind: step.kind, text: text, argument: argument, span: step.span))
  end
  return ok(
    Scenario(
      name: name,
      steps: expanded,
      tags: tags.concat(row.tags),
      span: draft.span,
      example: Report.Example.Row(row.span),
    ),
  )
end

def substitute_argument(argument: Argument, bindings: Map[String, String]) -> Result[Argument]
  case argument
    Argument.DocString(text) -> return ok(Argument.DocString(try substitute(text, bindings)))
    Argument.DataTable(rows) ->
      replaced: List[List[String]] = []
      for cells in rows
        replaced = replaced.push(try collect(cells.map do |cell| substitute(cell, bindings) end))
      end
      return ok(Argument.DataTable(replaced))
    Argument.NoArgument -> return ok(argument)
  end
end

# Replaces each <name> (no < or > inside) from the left; the error is the first unknown name.
def substitute(text: String, bindings: Map[String, String]) -> Result[String]
  if not text.include?("<")
    return ok(text)
  end
  parts = text.split("<")
  pieces = collect(parts.drop(1).map do |part| substitute_part(part, bindings) end)
  if not pieces.ok?
    return error(pieces.message)
  end
  return ok(parts[0] + pieces.unwrap!.join(""))
end

def substitute_part(part: String, bindings: Map[String, String]) -> Result[String]
  close = part.index_of(">").unwrap_or(0)
  if close == 0
    return ok("<#{part}")
  end
  name = part.slice(0, close)
  if not bindings.has_key?(name)
    return error(name)
  end
  return ok(bindings[name] + rest_of(part, close + 1))
end

## Matches step text against step patterns for `agentica test`.
##
## A pattern is plain text with `{string}` and `{int}` placeholders.

import Gherkin from "gherkin"
import Report from "std/test/report"

enum Capture
  IntCapture
  StringCapture
end

struct Slot
  capture: Capture
  literal: List[String]
end

## A compiled step pattern. `compile` builds them.
export struct Pattern
  text: String
  head: List[String]
  slots: List[Slot]
end

## The pattern a step matched: its index in the list and the values it captured.
export struct Resolved
  index: Int
  captures: List[String]
end

## Compiles the step patterns `texts`. Checks them in order and returns a failure at `where` for the first duplicate
## (`RUNTIME-BDD-DUPLICATE`) or bad pattern (`RUNTIME-BDD-PATTERN`).
export def compile(texts: List[String], where: Report.Span) -> Gherkin.Outcome[List[Pattern]]
  compiled = texts.map do |text| compile_one(text) end
  seen: Map[String, Bool] = {}
  for i in 0...texts.size
    text = texts[i]
    if seen.has_key?(text)
      return failed("RUNTIME-BDD-DUPLICATE", "duplicate step pattern", text, where)
    end
    if not compiled[i].ok?
      return failed("RUNTIME-BDD-PATTERN", compiled[i].message, text, where)
    end
    seen = seen.put(text, true)
  end
  return Gherkin.Outcome.Done(compiled.map do |pattern| pattern.unwrap! end)
end

## Finds the one pattern that matches the text of `step`. Fails with `CHECK-BDD-UNDEFINED` when none does and
## `CHECK-BDD-AMBIGUOUS` when several do.
export def resolve(patterns: List[Pattern], step: Gherkin.Step) -> Gherkin.Outcome[Resolved]
  found = patterns.map do |pattern| captures(pattern, step.text) end
  hits = 0
  first = 0
  for i in 0...found.size
    if found[i].ok?
      if hits == 0
        first = i
      end
      hits += 1
    end
  end
  if hits == 0
    return Gherkin.Outcome.Failed(
      Gherkin.Diagnostic(code: "CHECK-BDD-UNDEFINED", message: "no step definition matches", span: step.span),
    )
  end
  if hits > 1
    return Gherkin.Outcome.Failed(
      Gherkin.Diagnostic(code: "CHECK-BDD-AMBIGUOUS", message: "multiple step definitions match", span: step.span),
    )
  end
  return Gherkin.Outcome.Done(Resolved(index: first, captures: found[first].unwrap!))
end

## Matches `text` against `pattern`. Returns the captured values as strings, or an error when the text does not match.
export def captures(pattern: Pattern, text: String) -> Result[List[String]]
  chars = text.split("")
  if not literal_at?(chars, 0, pattern.head)
    return error("no match")
  end
  return walk(pattern.slots, 0, chars, pattern.head.size, [])
end

def failed(code: String, reason: String, text: String, where: Report.Span) -> Gherkin.Outcome[List[Pattern]]
  return Gherkin.Outcome.Failed(Gherkin.Diagnostic(code: code, message: "#{reason}: #{text}", span: where))
end

# Each "{" opens a placeholder only when the next brace is a "}".
def compile_one(text: String) -> Result[Pattern]
  parts = text.split("{")
  tails = parts.drop(1)
  for tail in tails
    close = tail.index_of("}")
    if close.ok? and not placeholder?(tail.slice(0, close.unwrap!))
      return error("only {string} and {int} are supported")
    end
  end
  if parts[0].include?("}")
    return error("unmatched pattern braces")
  end
  for tail in tails
    close = tail.index_of("}")
    if not close.ok? or after(tail, close.unwrap!).include?("}")
      return error("unmatched pattern braces")
    end
  end
  slots = tails.map do |tail|
    close = tail.index_of("}").unwrap!
    capture = Capture.StringCapture
    if tail.slice(0, close) == "int"
      capture = Capture.IntCapture
    end
    Slot(capture: capture, literal: after(tail, close).split(""))
  end
  return ok(Pattern(text: text, head: parts[0].split(""), slots: slots))
end

def placeholder?(kind: String) -> Bool
  return kind == "string" or kind == "int"
end

def after(text: String, close: Int) -> String
  return text.slice(close + 1, text.length - close - 1)
end

def literal_at?(chars: List[String], at: Int, literal: List[String]) -> Bool
  if at + literal.size > chars.size
    return false
  end
  for i in 0...literal.size
    if chars[at + i] != literal[i]
      return false
    end
  end
  return true
end

# Tries the captures from the regular expression's order: {int} from its longest to its shortest.
def walk(slots: List[Slot], k: Int, chars: List[String], at: Int, found: List[String]) -> Result[List[String]]
  if k == slots.size
    if at == chars.size
      return ok(found)
    end
    return error("no match")
  end
  slot = slots[k]
  case slot.capture
    Capture.StringCapture ->
      stop = quoted_end(chars, at)
      if stop > at and literal_at?(chars, stop, slot.literal)
        return walk(slots, k + 1, chars, stop + slot.literal.size, found.push(unquote(chars, at, stop)))
      end
    Capture.IntCapture ->
      start = at
      if at < chars.size and chars[at] == "-"
        start = at + 1
      end
      stop = start
      while stop < chars.size and "0123456789".include?(chars[stop])
        stop += 1
      end
      while stop > start
        if literal_at?(chars, stop, slot.literal)
          value = chars.take(stop).drop(at).join("")
          result = walk(slots, k + 1, chars, stop + slot.literal.size, found.push(value))
          if result.ok?
            return result
          end
        end
        stop -= 1
      end
  end
  return error("no match")
end

# The index after the closing quote, or `at` when there is no quoted string there.
def quoted_end(chars: List[String], at: Int) -> Int
  if at >= chars.size or (chars[at] != "\"" and chars[at] != "'")
    return at
  end
  quote = chars[at]
  i = at + 1
  while i < chars.size
    if chars[i] == quote
      return i + 1
    end
    if chars[i] == "\\"
      i += 1
    end
    i += 1
  end
  return at
end

# Splitting on escaped backslashes first leaves each other backslash just before the character it escapes.
def unquote(chars: List[String], at: Int, stop: Int) -> String
  content = chars.take(stop - 1).drop(at + 1).join("")
  if not content.include?("\\")
    return content
  end
  return content.split("\\\\").map do |part| part.replace("\\", "") end.join("\\")
end

## Reads and writes binary numbers in a `List[Int]` of bytes.
##
## Import it with `import Binary from "std/binary"`. Binary data is a `List[Int]` with each item in `0 .. 255`, like
## `IO.read_bytes` and `File.read_bytes` give. A reader takes a zero-based `offset` and returns a `Result`; it never
## halts. A writer returns a new list with exactly the bytes of its type. `_be` is big-endian (most significant byte
## first, network order) and `_le` is little-endian. Signed types use two's complement. A `u64` above
## `9223372036854775807` is not an `Int`: use `read_i64_be` and `write_i64_be` for all 64 bits.

## Reads an unsigned 8-bit integer at `offset`. Returns an error when the bytes are outside `data` or an item is not a
## byte.
export def read_u8(data: List[Int], offset: Int) -> Result[Int]
  return load8(data, offset, "u8")
end

## Reads a signed 8-bit integer at `offset`. Returns an error when the bytes are outside `data` or an item is not a
## byte.
export def read_i8(data: List[Int], offset: Int) -> Result[Int]
  value = try load8(data, offset, "i8")
  return ok(extend(value, 8))
end

## Reads a big-endian unsigned 16-bit integer at `offset`. Returns an error when the bytes are outside `data` or an
## item is not a byte.
export def read_u16_be(data: List[Int], offset: Int) -> Result[Int]
  return load16_be(data, offset, "u16")
end

## Reads a little-endian unsigned 16-bit integer at `offset`. Returns an error when the bytes are outside `data` or an
## item is not a byte.
export def read_u16_le(data: List[Int], offset: Int) -> Result[Int]
  return load16_le(data, offset, "u16")
end

## Reads a big-endian signed 16-bit integer at `offset`. Returns an error when the bytes are outside `data` or an item
## is not a byte.
export def read_i16_be(data: List[Int], offset: Int) -> Result[Int]
  value = try load16_be(data, offset, "i16")
  return ok(extend(value, 16))
end

## Reads a little-endian signed 16-bit integer at `offset`. Returns an error when the bytes are outside `data` or an
## item is not a byte.
export def read_i16_le(data: List[Int], offset: Int) -> Result[Int]
  value = try load16_le(data, offset, "i16")
  return ok(extend(value, 16))
end

## Reads a big-endian unsigned 32-bit integer at `offset`. Returns an error when the bytes are outside `data` or an
## item is not a byte.
export def read_u32_be(data: List[Int], offset: Int) -> Result[Int]
  return load32_be(data, offset, "u32")
end

## item is not a byte.
export def read_u32_le(data: List[Int], offset: Int) -> Result[Int]

end

## Reads a big-endian signed 32-bit integer at `offset`. Returns an error when the bytes are outside `data` or an item
## is not a byte.
export def read_i32_be(data: List[Int], offset: Int) -> Result[Int]

end

## Reads a little-endian signed 32-bit integer at `offset`. Returns an error when the bytes are outside `data` or an
## item is not a byte.
export def read_i32_le(data: List[Int], offset: Int) -> Result[Int]
  value = try load32_le(data, offset, "i32")
  return ok(extend(value, 32))
end

## Reads a big-endian unsigned 64-bit integer at `offset`. Returns an error when the bytes are outside `data` or an
## item is not a byte, or when the value is above `9223372036854775807`.
export def read_u64_be(data: List[Int], offset: Int) -> Result[Int]
  value = try load64_be(data, offset, "u64")

end

## Reads a little-endian unsigned 64-bit integer at `offset`. Returns an error when the bytes are outside `data` or an

export def read_u64_le(data: List[Int], offset: Int) -> Result[Int]

## Reads a big-endian signed 64-bit integer at `offset`. Returns an error when the bytes are outside `data` or an item
## is not a byte.
export def read_i64_be(data: List[Int], offset: Int) -> Result[Int]
  return load64_be(data, offset, "i64")
end

## Reads a little-endian signed 64-bit integer at `offset`. Returns an error when the bytes are outside `data` or an
## item is not a byte.
export def read_i64_le(data: List[Int], offset: Int) -> Result[Int]
  return load64_le(data, offset, "i64")
end

## Reads a big-endian 32-bit IEEE 754 float at `offset`. Returns an error when the bytes are outside `data` or an item
## is not a byte.
export def read_f32_be(data: List[Int], offset: Int) -> Result[Float]
  bits = try load32_be(data, offset, "f32")
  return ok(Float.from_bits32(bits))
end

## Reads a little-endian 32-bit IEEE 754 float at `offset`. Returns an error when the bytes are outside `data` or an
## item is not a byte.
export def read_f32_le(data: List[Int], offset: Int) -> Result[Float]
  bits = try load32_le(data, offset, "f32")
  return ok(Float.from_bits32(bits))
end

## Reads a big-endian 64-bit IEEE 754 float at `offset`. Returns an error when the bytes are outside `data` or an item
## is not a byte.
export def read_f64_be(data: List[Int], offset: Int) -> Result[Float]
  bits = try load64_be(data, offset, "f64")
  return ok(Float.from_bits(bits))
end

## Reads a little-endian 64-bit IEEE 754 float at `offset`. Returns an error when the bytes are outside `data` or an
## item is not a byte.
export def read_f64_le(data: List[Int], offset: Int) -> Result[Float]
  bits = try load64_le(data, offset, "f64")
  return ok(Float.from_bits(bits))
end

## Returns the 1 byte of `value` as an unsigned 8-bit integer. Returns an error when `value` is not in `0 .. 255`.
export def write_u8(value: Int) -> Result[List[Int]]
  try fits(value, 0, 255, "u8")
  return ok([value])
end

## Returns the 1 byte of `value` as a signed 8-bit integer. Returns an error when `value` is not in `-128 .. 127`.
export def write_i8(value: Int) -> Result[List[Int]]
  try fits(value, -128, 127, "i8")
  return ok([value.bit_and(255)])

    return error("frame limit #{max} is negative")
  end
  length = try load32_be(data, offset, "u32")

def first_bad_byte(data: List[Int], offset: Int, n: Int) -> Result[Void]

  stop = offset + n
  while i < stop

      return error("value #{b} at index #{i} is not a byte")
    end

  end
  return ok()
end

def bytes_ok(data: List[Int], offset: Int, n: Int, combined: Int) -> Result[Void]

def extend(value: Int, bits: Int) -> Int

  b = data[offset + 1]

def load32_be(data: List[Int], offset: Int, type: String) -> Result[Int]

  a = data[offset]

  b = data[offset + 1]
  c = data[offset + 2]
  d = data[offset + 3]
  e = data[offset + 4]
  f = data[offset + 5]
  g = data[offset + 6]

  high = h.shift_left(24).bit_or(g.shift_left(16)).bit_or(f.shift_left(8)).bit_or(e)
  return ok(high.shift_left(32).bit_or(low))

def unsigned64(value: Int, offset: Int) -> Result[Int]
  if value < 0
    return error("u64 at offset #{offset} does not fit in Int")
  end
  return ok(value)
end

def bytes2_be(value: Int) -> List[Int]
  return [value.shift_right(8).bit_and(255), value.bit_and(255)]
end

def bytes2_le(value: Int) -> List[Int]
  return [value.bit_and(255), value.shift_right(8).bit_and(255)]
end

def bytes4_be(value: Int) -> List[Int]
  return [
    value.shift_right(24).bit_and(255),
    value.shift_right(16).bit_and(255),
    value.shift_right(8).bit_and(255),
    value.bit_and(255),
  ]
end

def bytes4_le(value: Int) -> List[Int]
  return [
    value.bit_and(255),
    value.shift_right(8).bit_and(255),
    value.shift_right(16).bit_and(255),
    value.shift_right(24).bit_and(255),
  ]
end

def bytes8_be(value: Int) -> List[Int]
  return [
    value.shift_right(56).bit_and(255),
    value.shift_right(48).bit_and(255),
    value.shift_right(40).bit_and(255),
    value.shift_right(32).bit_and(255),
    value.shift_right(24).bit_and(255),
    value.shift_right(16).bit_and(255),
    value.shift_right(8).bit_and(255),
    value.bit_and(255),
  ]
end

def bytes8_le(value: Int) -> List[Int]
  return [
    value.bit_and(255),
    value.shift_right(8).bit_and(255),
    value.shift_right(16).bit_and(255),
    value.shift_right(24).bit_and(255),
    value.shift_right(32).bit_and(255),
    value.shift_right(40).bit_and(255),
    value.shift_right(48).bit_and(255),
    value.shift_right(56).bit_and(255),
  ]
end

def join_parts(parts: List[List[Int]], first: Int, stop: Int) -> List[Int]
  count = stop - first
  if count == 0
    return []
  end
  if count == 1
    return parts[first]
  end
  middle = first + count / 2
  return List.concat(join_parts(parts, first, middle), join_parts(parts, middle, stop))
end

## An HTTP/1.1 client and server.
##
## Import it with `import HTTP from "std/http"`. Every call is whole: it returns after the whole response arrived, and
## the body is a `String`. Status codes such as 404 or 500 are normal responses. A bad URL, a refused connection, a
## timeout or a body over the limit is an `error` result.

READ_BYTES = 65536
# Chunked framing is read in small pieces, since chunk data goes straight into text.
FRAME_BYTES = 512
SMALL_BODY = 16384
TEXT_BYTES = 1048576
BAD_TEXT = "400 request body is not valid UTF-8"
# The least time an error answer gets to be sent, even past the request deadline.
ANSWER_MS = 100

struct Target
  scheme: String
  host: String
  port: Int
  target: String
end

struct Service
  server: HttpServer
  handler: Fn[HttpRequest, Result[HttpResponse]]
  options: HttpServerOptions
end

struct Incoming
  request: HttpRequest
  rest: List[Int]
end

struct Body
  pieces: List[String]
  carry: List[Int]
end

struct Reading
  socket: Socket
  head: HttpWire.Head
  deadline: Int
  max_body_bytes: Int
end

## Returns the default client options: 30 s timeouts, up to 4 connections, 1 MiB bodies and the system CA certificates.
export def client_options() -> HttpClientOptions
  return HttpClientOptions(
    timeout_ms: 30000,
    idle_timeout_ms: 30000,
    max_connections: 4,
    max_body_bytes: 1048576,
    ca_file: "",
  )
end

## Creates a client that keeps connections open and reuses them. Every number in `options` must be positive,
## `max_connections` at most 65536 and `max_body_bytes` at most 64 MiB, or the result is an error. Close the client
## with `close_client`.
export def client(options: HttpClientOptions) -> Result[HttpClient]
  try check_options(options.timeout_ms, options.idle_timeout_ms, options.max_connections, options.max_body_bytes)
  return HttpWire.client(
    options.timeout_ms,
    options.idle_timeout_ms,
    options.max_connections,
    options.max_body_bytes,
    options.ca_file,
  )
end

## Closes the client and its connections. A call still in flight fails.
export def close_client(pool: HttpClient) -> Void
  HttpWire.close_client(pool)
end

## Sends a `GET` request to `url` and returns the response.
export def get(pool: HttpClient, url: String) -> Result[HttpResponse]
  return request(pool, "GET", url, [], "")
end

## Sends a `POST` request to `url` with `headers` and the text `body`.
export def post(pool: HttpClient, url: String, headers: List[Header], body: String) -> Result[HttpResponse]
  return request(pool, "POST", url, headers, body)
end

## Sends a request with any `method`. `url` must start with `http://` or `https://`.
## The client adds `Host` and `Content-Length` itself, so `headers` may not set them, nor `Transfer-Encoding` or
## `Connection`.
export def request(
  pool: HttpClient,
  method: String,
  url: String,
  headers: List[Header],
  body: String,
) -> Result[HttpResponse]
  where = try parse_url(url)
  return HttpWire.exchange(pool, where.scheme, where.host, where.port, method, where.target, headers, body)
end

## Returns every value of the header `name`, ignoring case, in order.
export def header_values(headers: List[Header], name: String) -> List[String]
  wanted = String.downcase(name)
  found: List[String] = []
  for header in headers
    if String.downcase(header.name) == wanted
      found = List.append(found, header.value)
    end
  end
  return found
end

## Returns the default server options: 30 s `request_timeout_ms` and `idle_timeout_ms`, 128 connections and 1 MiB
## bodies.
export def server_options() -> HttpServerOptions
  return HttpServerOptions(
    request_timeout_ms: 30000,
    idle_timeout_ms: 30000,
    max_connections: 128,
    max_body_bytes: 1048576,
  )
end

## Starts an HTTP server on `host` and `port` and returns at once; it serves in the background. `handler` takes the
## whole request and returns the whole response. Port 0 picks a free port, which `local_port` returns. The server
## closes when the task that called `listen` ends.
export def listen(
  host: String,
  port: Int,
  handler: Fn[HttpRequest, Result[HttpResponse]],
  options: HttpServerOptions,
) -> Result[HttpServer]
  try check_options(
    options.request_timeout_ms,
    options.idle_timeout_ms,
    options.max_connections,
    options.max_body_bytes,
  )
  listener = try TCP.listen(host, port)
  return ok(start(listener, handler, options))
end

## Like `listen`, but over TLS, with the PEM certificate in `cert_file` and the key in `key_file`.
export def listen_tls(
  host: String,
  port: Int,
  cert_file: String,
  key_file: String,
  handler: Fn[HttpRequest, Result[HttpResponse]],
  options: HttpServerOptions,
) -> Result[HttpServer]
  try check_options(
    options.request_timeout_ms,
    options.idle_timeout_ms,
    options.max_connections,
    options.max_body_bytes,
  )
  listener = try TLS.listen(host, port, cert_file, key_file)
  return ok(start(listener, handler, options))
end

## Returns the port the server listens on.
export def local_port(server: HttpServer) -> Int
  return HttpWire.local_port(server)
end

## Waits until the server is closed, then returns `ok()`.
export def wait(server: HttpServer) -> Result[Void]
  return HttpWire.wait(server)
end

## Stops accepting, closes every connection and cancels the running handlers. Calling it again does nothing.
export def close_server(server: HttpServer) -> Void
  HttpWire.close_server(server)
end

def check_options(timeout_ms: Int, idle_timeout_ms: Int, max_connections: Int, max_body_bytes: Int) -> Result[Void]
  if timeout_ms <= 0 or idle_timeout_ms <= 0 or max_connections <= 0 or max_body_bytes <= 0
    return error("http: every option must be positive")
  end
  if max_connections > 65536
    return error("http: max_connections must be at most 65536")
  end
  if max_body_bytes > 67108864
    return error("http: max_body_bytes must be at most 67108864")
  end
  return ok()
end

def first_of(text: String, part: String) -> Int
  return Result.unwrap_or(String.index_of(text, part), String.length(text))
end

def rest_of(text: String, start: Int) -> String
  return String.slice(text, start, String.length(text) - start)
end

def plain?(text: String, digits_only: Bool) -> Bool
  for c in String.split(text, "")
    code = String.code(c)
    if code < 33 or code > 126 or (digits_only and (code < 48 or code > 57))
      return false
    end
  end
  return true
end

def ipv6?(text: String) -> Bool
  if not String.contains?(text, ":")
    return false
  end
  for c in String.split(text, "")
    code = String.code(c)
    if not ((code >= 48 and code <= 58) or (code >= 65 and code <= 70) or (code >= 97 and code <= 102) or code == 46)
      return false
    end
  end
  return true
end

def bad_url() -> Result[Target]
  return error("http: the URL must be http:// or https:// with a host, and without user info")
end

def parse_url(url: String) -> Result[Target]
  split = first_of(url, "://")
  scheme = String.downcase(String.slice(url, 0, split))
  if split == String.length(url) or (scheme != "http" and scheme != "https")
    return bad_url()
  end
  rest = rest_of(url, split + 3)
  rest = String.slice(rest, 0, first_of(rest, "#"))
  stop = first_of(rest, "/")
  query = first_of(rest, "?")
  if query < stop
    stop = query
  end
  authority = String.slice(rest, 0, stop)
  target = rest_of(rest, stop)
  if not String.starts_with?(target, "/")
    target = "/#{target}"
  end
  host = authority
  port_text = ""
  if String.starts_with?(authority, "[")
    close = first_of(authority, "]")
    if close == String.length(authority)
      return bad_url()
    end
    host = String.slice(authority, 1, close - 1)
    if not ipv6?(host)
      return bad_url()
    end
    after = rest_of(authority, close + 1)
    if after != ""
      if after == ":" or not String.starts_with?(after, ":")
        return bad_url()
      end
      port_text = rest_of(after, 1)
    end
  elsif String.contains?(authority, ":")
    colon = first_of(authority, ":")
    host = String.slice(authority, 0, colon)
    port_text = rest_of(authority, colon + 1)
    if port_text == ""
      return bad_url()
    end
  end
  if host == "" or String.contains?(authority, "@") or not plain?(host, false) or not plain?(port_text, true)
    return bad_url()
  end
  port = 80
  if scheme == "https"
    port = 443
  end
  if String.length(port_text) > 5
    return error("http: the port must be 1..65535")
  end
  if port_text != ""
    port = String.to_int!(port_text)
  end
  if port < 1 or port > 65535
    return error("http: the port must be 1..65535")
  end
  return ok(Target(scheme: scheme, host: String.downcase(host), port: port, target: target))
end

def start(listener: Listener, handler: Fn[HttpRequest, Result[HttpResponse]], options: HttpServerOptions) -> HttpServer
  return HttpWire.server(listener, options.max_connections) do |server|
    accept_all(Service(server: server, handler: handler, options: options))
  end
end

def accept_all(service: Service) -> Void
  while true
    case HttpWire.accept(service.server)
      ok(socket) -> HttpWire.spawn(service.server, socket) do |s| serve(s, service) end
      error(_) -> return
    end
  end
end

def serve(socket: Socket, service: Service) -> Void
  options = service.options
  wait_ms = options.request_timeout_ms
  rest: List[Int] = []
  while true
    case read_request(socket, rest, wait_ms, options)
      ok(incoming) ->
        if not answer(socket, incoming.request, service)
          return
        end
        rest = incoming.rest
      error(_) -> return
    end
    wait_ms = options.idle_timeout_ms
  end
end

# One whole request. rest holds the bytes the last chunked body read past its end. The first byte may take first_ms;
# then the rest of the request has request_timeout_ms. A request that breaks the rules gets its error answer here, and
# the result is the error.
def read_request(socket: Socket, rest: List[Int], first_ms: Int, options: HttpServerOptions) -> Result[Incoming]
  first = rest
  if List.size(first) == 0
    first = try TCP.recv_bytes(socket, 1, first_ms)
    if List.size(first) == 0
      return error("network: end of input")
    end
  end
  deadline = Time.monotonic_ms() + options.request_timeout_ms
  head = try read_head(socket, first, deadline, options.max_body_bytes)
  reading = Reading(socket: socket, head: head, deadline: deadline, max_body_bytes: options.max_body_bytes)
  if head.expect_continue and (head.chunked or head.length > 0) and head.buffered == 0
    try TCP.send(socket, "HTTP/1.1 100 Continue\r\n\r\n", try time_left(socket, deadline))
  end
  if head.chunked
    return read_chunked(reading)
  end
  return read_length(reading)
end

# The head stays in the socket's input until it is whole (HttpWire.read_head), so a slow head holds no List here.
def read_head(socket: Socket, rest: List[Int], deadline: Int, max_body_bytes: Int) -> Result[HttpWire.Head]
  left = try time_left(socket, deadline)
  case HttpWire.read_head(socket, rest, max_body_bytes, left)
    ok(head) ->
      if head.status > 0
        return error(refuse(socket, head.status, head.reason, deadline))
      end
      return ok(head)
    error(message) ->
      TCP.close(socket)
      return error(message)
  end
end

def read_length(reading: Reading) -> Result[Incoming]
  body = Body(pieces: [], carry: [])
  left = reading.head.length
  while left > 0
    piece = try more_text(reading, body.carry, smaller(left, TEXT_BYTES))
    body = Body(pieces: List.append(body.pieces, piece.text), carry: piece.carry)
    left = left - piece.bytes
  end
  return finish(reading, body, [])
end

def read_chunked(reading: Reading) -> Result[Incoming]
  data: List[Int] = []
  state = HttpWire.chunked(reading.max_body_bytes)
  body = Body(pieces: [], carry: [])
  while not state.done
    if state.remaining > 0
      # The rest of a chunk goes straight into text; only framing goes through the decoder.
      piece = try more_text(reading, body.carry, smaller(state.remaining, TEXT_BYTES))
      body = Body(pieces: List.append(body.pieces, piece.text), carry: piece.carry)
      state = HttpWire.chunk_read(state, piece.bytes)
    else
      # A small read: chunk data past the framing is read as text above.
      data = try more_request(reading.socket, FRAME_BYTES, reading.deadline)
      state = try next_chunk(reading, state, data)
      body = try add_text(reading, body, data, state.runs)
    end
  end
  return finish(reading, body, List.drop(data, state.next))
end

def next_chunk(reading: Reading, state: HttpWire.Chunk, data: List[Int]) -> Result[HttpWire.Chunk]
  case HttpWire.chunk(state, data, 0)
    ok(next) -> return ok(next)
    error(problem) -> return error(refuse_problem(reading.socket, problem, reading.deadline))
  end
end

# Adds the runs of data to the body text; an unfinished character waits in carry for the next bytes.
def add_text(reading: Reading, body: Body, data: List[Int], runs: List[Int]) -> Result[Body]
  piece = HttpWire.text(body.carry, data, runs)
  if not piece.valid
    return error(refuse_problem(reading.socket, BAD_TEXT, reading.deadline))
  end
  return ok(Body(pieces: List.append(body.pieces, piece.text), carry: piece.carry))
end

# The next bytes of a body, read straight into text.
def more_text(reading: Reading, carry: List[Int], most: Int) -> Result[HttpWire.Text]
  left = try time_left(reading.socket, reading.deadline)
  piece = try HttpWire.read_text(reading.socket, most, carry, left)
  if not piece.valid
    return error(refuse_problem(reading.socket, BAD_TEXT, reading.deadline))
  end
  if piece.bytes == 0
    TCP.close(reading.socket)
    return error("http: connection closed before the request was complete")
  end
  return ok(piece)
end

def finish(reading: Reading, body: Body, rest: List[Int]) -> Result[Incoming]
  if List.size(body.carry) > 0
    return error(refuse_problem(reading.socket, BAD_TEXT, reading.deadline))
  end
  head = reading.head
  request = HttpRequest(
    method: head.method,
    target: head.target,
    path: head.path,
    headers: head.headers,
    body: String.join(body.pieces, ""),
  )
  return ok(Incoming(request: request, rest: rest))
end

def smaller(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
  if a < b
    return a
  end
  return b
end

# The next bytes of a request that has started: the end of input here closes the connection with no answer.
def more_request(socket: Socket, most: Int, deadline: Int) -> Result[List[Int]]
  data = try TCP.recv_bytes(socket, most, try time_left(socket, deadline))
  if List.size(data) == 0
    TCP.close(socket)
    return error("http: connection closed before the request was complete")
  end
  return ok(data)
end

# The milliseconds left before deadline. When none are left the socket closes, as a timeout in TCP closes it.
def time_left(socket: Socket, deadline: Int) -> Result[Int]
  left = deadline - Time.monotonic_ms()
  if left <= 0
    TCP.close(socket)
    return error("network: operation timed out")
  end
  return ok(left)
end

# Answers a bad request, closes, and returns the error text.
def refuse(socket: Socket, status: Int, reason: String, deadline: Int) -> String
  linger(socket, HttpWire.error_answer(status), deadline)
  return "http: #{reason}"
end

# refuse for a problem written "NNN reason" (HttpWire.chunk, BAD_TEXT): NNN is the answer's status.
def refuse_problem(socket: Socket, problem: String, deadline: Int) -> String
  return refuse(socket, String.to_int!(String.slice(problem, 0, 3)), rest_of(problem, 4), deadline)
end

# Sends text, closes the write side, and reads and drops input until the peer closes or deadline, so unread request
# bytes cannot turn the close into a reset that loses the answer. Then it closes the socket. The answer gets at least
# ANSWER_MS even when the deadline has passed; only the drain is bound by the deadline.
def linger(socket: Socket, text: String, deadline: Int) -> Void
  wait = deadline - Time.monotonic_ms()
  if wait < ANSWER_MS
    wait = ANSWER_MS
  end
  if text == "" or Result.ok?(TCP.send(socket, text, wait))
    HttpWire.close_write(socket)
    drain(socket, deadline)
  end
  TCP.close(socket)
end

def drain(socket: Socket, deadline: Int) -> Void
  while true
    case time_left(socket, deadline)
      ok(left) ->
        case TCP.recv_bytes(socket, READ_BYTES, left)
          ok(data) ->
            if List.size(data) == 0
              return
            end
          error(_) -> return
        end
      error(_) -> return
    end
  end
end

def answer(socket: Socket, request: HttpRequest, service: Service) -> Bool
  timeout = service.options.request_timeout_ms
  case service.handler.call(request)
    ok(response) ->
      case write_response(socket, request, response, timeout)
        ok(keep) -> return keep
        error(message) ->
          if String.starts_with?(message, "http: invalid response: ")
            IO.warn(message)
            failed(socket, request, timeout)
          end
      end
    error(message) ->
      IO.warn("http: handler error: #{message}")
      failed(socket, request, timeout)
  end
  return false
end

# Writes one whole response with Content-Length. ok(false) when the request or the response asked to close: the
# connection then closes as in linger.
def write_response(socket: Socket, request: HttpRequest, response: HttpResponse, timeout: Int) -> Result[Bool]
  case HttpWire.encode_response(request, response, Time.now_ms())
    ok(reply) -> return send_response(socket, request, response, reply, timeout)
    error(reason) -> return error("http: invalid response: #{reason}")
  end
end

def send_response(
  socket: Socket,
  request: HttpRequest,
  response: HttpResponse,
  reply: HttpWire.Reply,
  timeout: Int,
) -> Result[Bool]
  deadline = Time.monotonic_ms() + timeout
  body = response.body
  if request.method == "HEAD"
    body = ""
  end
  case String.from_bytes(reply.head)
    ok(text) ->
      if String.length(body) <= SMALL_BODY
        try TCP.send(socket, text + body, timeout)
      else
        try TCP.send(socket, text, timeout)
        try TCP.send(socket, body, try time_left(socket, deadline))
      end
    error(_) ->
      try TCP.send_bytes(socket, reply.head, timeout)
      if body != ""
        try TCP.send(socket, body, try time_left(socket, deadline))
      end
  end
  if reply.closes
    linger(socket, "", deadline)
    return ok(false)
  end
  return ok(true)
end

def failed(socket: Socket, request: HttpRequest, timeout: Int) -> Void
  write_response(
    socket,
    request,
    HttpResponse(status: 500, headers: [Header(name: "Connection", value: "close")], body: ""),
    timeout,
  )
end

## An Elixir-style logger with four levels, one global level and named handlers.
##
## Import it with `import Logger from "std/logger"`. The levels are the builtin enum `LogLevel`
## (`Debug < Info < Warning < Error`) and a handler receives the builtin record `LogEvent`. The first call of any
## function here installs a handler named `console` (`stderr_text`, level `info`). Handlers run in order,
## synchronously, in the task that logs, so a line is written when the call returns. A handler error is the error of
## the task that logged. The registry lives in the VM and belongs to one run.

struct JsonLine
  time: String
  level: String
  msg: String
  fields: Map[String, String]
  task: Int
end

# A level function reads the floor once and compares it once. The floor is the higher of the global level and the
# lowest handler level, so a call that no handler would accept is as cheap as a disabled one: one user call, one
# builtin call and one comparison. -1 (the default not installed yet) is below every threshold, so it takes the slow
# path, where ready() installs the default and the real global level is checked.

## Logs a `debug` message.
export def debug(message: String) -> Void
  if LogRegistry.floor() <= 0
    if ready() <= 0
      dispatch(LogLevel.Debug, 0, message, {})
    end
  end
end

## Logs a `debug` message with fields.
export def debug_meta(message: String, fields: Map[String, String]) -> Void
  if LogRegistry.floor() <= 0
    if ready() <= 0
      dispatch(LogLevel.Debug, 0, message, fields)
    end
  end
end

## Logs an `info` message.
export def info(message: String) -> Void
  if LogRegistry.floor() <= 1
    if ready() <= 1
      dispatch(LogLevel.Info, 1, message, {})
    end
  end
end

## Logs an `info` message with fields.
export def info_meta(message: String, fields: Map[String, String]) -> Void
  if LogRegistry.floor() <= 1
    if ready() <= 1
      dispatch(LogLevel.Info, 1, message, fields)
    end
  end
end

## Logs a `warning` message.
export def warning(message: String) -> Void
  if LogRegistry.floor() <= 2
    if ready() <= 2
      dispatch(LogLevel.Warning, 2, message, {})
    end
  end
end

## Logs a `warning` message with fields.
export def warning_meta(message: String, fields: Map[String, String]) -> Void
  if LogRegistry.floor() <= 2
    if ready() <= 2
      dispatch(LogLevel.Warning, 2, message, fields)
    end
  end
end

## Logs an `error` message. The function is `err` because `error` is a reserved name; the output still says `error`.
export def err(message: String) -> Void
  if LogRegistry.floor() <= 3
    if ready() <= 3
      dispatch(LogLevel.Error, 3, message, {})
    end
  end
end

## Logs an `error` message with fields.
export def err_meta(message: String, fields: Map[String, String]) -> Void
  if LogRegistry.floor() <= 3
    if ready() <= 3
      dispatch(LogLevel.Error, 3, message, fields)
    end
  end
end

## Logs a message at a level given as a value.
export def log(level: LogLevel, message: String) -> Void
  return log_meta(level, message, {})
end

## Logs a message with fields at a level given as a value.
export def log_meta(level: LogLevel, message: String, fields: Map[String, String]) -> Void
  rank = rank_of(level)
  if rank >= ready()
    dispatch(level, rank, message, fields)
  end
end

## Returns true only when a call at `level` would reach a handler: the level is at or above the global level and at or
## above the lowest level of the attached handlers. Guard costly fields with it.
export def enabled?(level: LogLevel) -> Bool
  rank = rank_of(level)
  return rank >= ready() and rank >= LogRegistry.lowest()
end

## Returns the global level, `info` until `set_level` changes it.
export def level() -> LogLevel
  return level_of(ready())
end

## Sets the global level. A call below it makes no event at all.
export def set_level(level: LogLevel) -> Void
  _ = ready()
  LogRegistry.set_level(rank_of(level))
end

## Attaches a handler under a name, for events at `level` or above. The handler is a function (`&Logger.stderr_json`)
## or a block. A name already in use is an error result.
export def attach(name: String, level: LogLevel, handler: Fn[LogEvent, Void]) -> Result[Void]
  _ = ready()
  return LogRegistry.attach(name, rank_of(level), handler)
end

## Detaches the handler with that name. A name not in use is an error result.
export def detach(name: String) -> Result[Void]
  _ = ready()
  return LogRegistry.detach(name)
end

## Returns the names of the attached handlers, in attach order.
export def handlers() -> List[String]
  _ = ready()
  return LogRegistry.names()
end

## Writes `format_text(event)` to stderr as one line.
export def stderr_text(event: LogEvent) -> Void
  IO.warn(format_text(event))
end

## Writes `format_json(event)` to stderr as one line.
export def stderr_json(event: LogEvent) -> Void
  IO.warn(format_json(event))
end

## Returns the text line of an event: `TIME LEVEL MESSAGE key=value ...`, with the time in UTC.
## A message or field that is empty, has a space (for a field), `=`, a quote, a backslash or a control character is
## written as a JSON string, so a line is always one line.
export def format_text(event: LogEvent) -> String
  parts = [time_text(event.time_ms), level_name(event.level).upcase, message_token(event.message)]
  for key in event.fields.keys
    parts = parts.push("#{field_token(key)}=#{field_token(event.fields.get(key, ""))}")
  end
  return parts.join(" ")
end

## Returns the JSON line of an event: the keys `time`, `level`, `msg`, `fields` and `task`. The fields are nested, so a
## field named `level` never clashes with a fixed key.
export def format_json(event: LogEvent) -> String
  return one_line(
    JSON.encode(
      JsonLine(
        time: time_text(event.time_ms),
        level: level_name(event.level),
        msg: event.message,
        fields: event.fields,
        task: event.task,
      ),
    ),
  )
end

## Returns milliseconds since the Unix epoch as UTC text, such as `2026-10-12T10:15:02.345Z`.
## A year outside 0 to 9999 is written with its sign and at least four digits.
export def time_text(ms: Int) -> String
  # Floor division written so that no intermediate product leaves the Int range, even at Int.min.
  days = ms / 86400000
  rest = ms % 86400000
  if rest < 0
    days -= 1
    rest += 86400000
  end
  # Days to a calendar date by eras of 400 years, counted from 0000-03-01 so the leap day ends the year.
  z = days + 719468
  era = z / 146097
  if z % 146097 < 0
    era -= 1
  end
  doe = z - era * 146097
  yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36524 - doe / 146096) / 365
  doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100)
  shifted = (5 * doy + 2) / 153
  day = doy - (153 * shifted + 2) / 5 + 1
  month = shifted + 3
  year = yoe + era * 400
  if shifted >= 10
    month = shifted - 9
    year += 1
  end
  sign = ""
  if year < 0
    sign = "-"
    year = 0 - year
  end
  hour = rest / 3600000
  minute = rest % 3600000 / 60000
  second = rest % 60000 / 1000
  milli = rest % 1000
  date = "#{sign}#{pad(year, 4)}-#{pad(month, 2)}-#{pad(day, 2)}"
  clock = "#{pad(hour, 2)}:#{pad(minute, 2)}:#{pad(second, 2)}.#{pad(milli, 3)}"
  return "#{date}T#{clock}Z"
end

# The ranks are the order of LogLevel: debug 0, info 1, warning 2, error 3. LogRegistry stores ranks, not enums,
# so its rows need no enum type.
def rank_of(level: LogLevel) -> Int
  case level
    LogLevel.Debug -> return 0
    LogLevel.Info -> return 1
    LogLevel.Warning -> return 2
    LogLevel.Error -> return 3
  end
end

def level_of(rank: Int) -> LogLevel
  case rank
    0 -> return LogLevel.Debug
    1 -> return LogLevel.Info
    2 -> return LogLevel.Warning
    _ -> return LogLevel.Error
  end
end

def level_name(level: LogLevel) -> String
  case level
    LogLevel.Debug -> return "debug"
    LogLevel.Info -> return "info"
    LogLevel.Warning -> return "warning"
    LogLevel.Error -> return "error"
  end
end

# The install is one native call that checks for -1 itself, so two tasks that log for the first time together
# install the console handler once, and a later detach("console") stays in effect.
def ready() -> Int
  current = LogRegistry.level()
  if current < 0
    LogRegistry.install_default(&stderr_text)
    return LogRegistry.level()
  end
  return current
end

# The event takes its handlers here, so a handler that attaches or detaches another does not change this event.
# The event is made only when some handler accepts it.
def dispatch(level: LogLevel, rank: Int, message: String, fields: Map[String, String]) -> Void
  accepting = LogRegistry.handlers(rank)
  if accepting.size == 0
    return
  end
  event = LogEvent(level: level, message: message, fields: fields, time_ms: Time.now_ms(), task: LogRegistry.task_id())
  for handler in accepting
    handler.call(event)
  end
end

# JSON.encode(s) is the quoted, escaped text, so it equals "\"" + s + "\"" exactly when s has no quote, backslash
# or control character (DEL included). The three line breaks above are not escaped by it, so they are checked apart.
def plain?(text: String) -> Bool
  return text.length > 0 and !text.contains?("=") and !line_break?(text) and JSON.encode(text) == "\"#{text}\""
end

# JSON.encode leaves U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029 as they are, but splitlines() and some viewers break lines there.
# Escaping them keeps one event on one line.
def one_line(text: String) -> String
  return (
    text.replace(String.from_code(133), "\\u0085")
      .replace(String.from_code(8232), "\\u2028")
      .replace(String.from_code(8233), "\\u2029")
  )
end

def line_break?(text: String) -> Bool
  return (
    text.contains?(String.from_code(133)) or
    text.contains?(String.from_code(8232)) or
    text.contains?(String.from_code(8233))
  )
end

def message_token(message: String) -> String
  if plain?(message) and !message.starts_with?(" ") and !message.ends_with?(" ")
    return message
  end
  return one_line(JSON.encode(message))
end

def field_token(text: String) -> String
  if plain?(text) and !text.contains?(" ")
    return text
  end
  return one_line(JSON.encode(text))
end

def pad(n: Int, width: Int) -> String
  text = n.to_s
  while text.length < width
    text = "0#{text}"
  end
  return text
end

## An immutable first-in, first-out queue of strings.
##
## Every function returns a new queue and leaves the one you pass in unchanged. The queue is a `List` underneath; there
## is no native queue.

## A queue. Build one with `new`.
export struct QueueState
  ## The values, oldest first.
  items: List[String]
end

## What `pop` returns: the oldest value and the queue without it.
export struct Popped
  ## The oldest value.
  value: String
  ## The queue after the value was removed.
  remaining: QueueState
end

## Returns an empty queue.
export def new() -> QueueState
  return QueueState(items: [])
end

## Returns a queue with `value` added at the back.
export def push(q: QueueState, value: String) -> QueueState
  return QueueState(items: List.append(q.items, value))
end

## Takes the oldest value. Returns it with the rest of the queue, or an error when the queue is empty.
export def pop(q: QueueState) -> Result[Popped]
  if empty?(q)
    return error("queue is empty")
  end
  return ok(Popped(value: q.items[0], remaining: QueueState(items: List.drop(q.items, 1))))
end

## Returns the oldest value without removing it, or an error when the queue is empty.
export def peek(q: QueueState) -> Result[String]
  if empty?(q)
    return error("queue is empty")
  end
  return ok(q.items[0])
end

## Returns how many values are in the queue.
export def size(q: QueueState) -> Int
  return List.size(q.items)
end

## Returns true when the queue has no values.
export def empty?(q: QueueState) -> Bool
  return size(q) == 0
end
